deep.reconstruction:
The page continues a table of decimal periods of fractions with prime denominator p (the previous page covers 373–401, the next 409–439). Gauss's convention, checked on every block here: a block headed p is the full period of the decimal expansion of n/p, starting at the first decimal place. The block for the cycle of 1 has n = 10, i.e. it is the period of 1/p read from its second digit; its first group always begins with 0. When 10 is not a primitive root mod p, the order f = ord_p(10) is less than p−1. The e = (p−1)/f cosets of the subgroup <10> in (Z/p)^* are then each written out. Their representatives (my identification, verified numerically) are 10·h^k with h^e ≡ 10 (mod p). So the cosets are generated by an e-th root of 10.

(1) p = 443. ord(10) = 221 and e = 2. This is consistent with (10/443) = (2/443)(5/443) = (−1)(−1) = +1 (my justification). Block A has 9+9+4 groups plus one digit = 221 digits; it is the period of 185/443 = 0.4176072234…. Block B is marked as the cycle of 1 and is the period of 10/443 = 0.0225733634… (the 1/443 period shifted one place). Here 185 ≡ 10·240 and 240^2 ≡ 10 (mod 443). The period length is odd, so there is no complementary half.

(2) p = 449. ord(10) = 32 and e = 14. The rows are numbered 1–13 and 0, each row 32 digits. Row k is the period of r_k/449 with r_k ≡ 10·34^k: r = 340, 335, 165, 222, 364, 253, 71, 169, 358, …, 135, and 10 for row 0. Moreover 34^14 ≡ 10 (mod 449). In each row, digits 17–32 are the 9-complements of digits 1–16 (Midy). For example, row 0 = 0222717149 2204899777 2828507795 10.

(3) p = 457. ord(10) = 152 and e = 3. The three 152-digit blocks are the periods of 355/457, 35/457 and 10/457. Here 355 ≡ 10·264, 35 ≡ 10·264^2 and 264^3 ≡ 10. Midy complementation holds at offset 76.

(4) p = 461. 10 is a primitive root. One block of 460 digits gives the period of 10/461. The second half is the 9-complement of the first: digits 231–240 are 9783080260, the complement of 0216919739.

(5) p = 463. ord(10) = 154 and e = 3. The blocks are the periods of 351/463, 421/463 and 10/463, with h = 174 and 174^3 ≡ 10. The final digits 3023 / 6133 / 4730 are consistent, and complementation holds at offset 77.

End checks (mine): the last two digits of the period of n/p equal −n·p^{-1} mod 100. This holds for every block (85, 70, 40, 10, 90, 23, 33, 30, 5, 0).

The marginal '(2268)' is the number of digits on the page: 442+448+456+460+462 = 2268. Likewise the previous page's (2316) = 372+378+382+388+396+400. The '19020' is probably a running total; it was not verified.
errors: p=457, second block (period of 35/457): Gauss ran on past the 150th digit, then struck out the overrun ('45…'). The strike-through also removes the two digits that were actually needed. The block as it stands has only 150 of 152 digits. The missing final digits are '45', since −35·457^{-1} ≡ 45 (mod 100).

p=449 row 3 and p=461 line 3 contain overwritten digits. The intended values agree with 165/449 = 0.3674832962… and with the 461 period (7483731019). No arithmetic errors were otherwise detected in the spot checks made.

results.what: Decimal periods of 1/p and of all coset representatives 10·h^k/p for p = 443, 449, 457, 461, 463, with ord_p(10) = 221, 32, 152, 460, 154
results.modern_name: Tables of periods of decimal fractions (cyclotomic coset decomposition of (Z/p)^* by <10>)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones arts. 312–318; table published posthumously in Werke II); also Burckhardt, Reuschle, Desmarest

results.what: Choice of coset generator h with h^e ≡ 10 (mod p): 240 for 443, 34 for 449, 264 for 457, 174 for 463
results.modern_name: Cosets of the subgroup generated by 10, indexed by a root of 10

results.what: Second half of an even-length period equals the 9-complement of the first half
results.usually_credited_to: E. Midy 1836 (known earlier, used by Gauss)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working sheet for Gauss's well-known table converting common fractions into decimals (Werke II). The content is computational and of a kind already known to be his.
